newsitem.title: INDIA: India soybean crop sown on record 5.5 mln hectares.
newsitem.headline: India soybean crop sown on record 5.5 mln hectares.

text.p: Sowing for India's 1997/98 (Nov-Oct) soybean crop has been completed on a record 5.5 million hectares after main growing regions received plentiful monsoon rains, traders said on Friday.
In 1996/97, five million hectares were under soybeans.

Traders said 4.1 million hectares had been sown to the crop in central India against a target of four million. The Soybean Processors Association of India (SOPA) has set a countrywide target of 5.7 million ha.
"Indian farmers preferred to increase the area under the crop because they got good prices in 1996/97," SOPA chairman Davish Jain told Reuters.
Traders said a second spell of monsoon rains had been beneficial and would help proper germination of seeds and reduce the need of resowing.
They said soybean arrivals were poor in the central city of Indore, the hub of India's soybean processing industry, due to the lean season.
Soybean was quoted at 10,500-10,800 rupees per tonne against 11,600-11,800 at the same time last year.

Export demand for Indian soymeal was dull due to poor availability, traders said. Soymeal for export was currently quoted at $265-$266 per tonne (free alongside ship) against about $267-269 per tonne this time last year.
